summary: Issei Suzuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University and later served as a professor there.
Issei Yamakawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sophia University and completed a master's program at Aichi Gakuin University.

István Tamaskó was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Vienna and the University of Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald, later becoming a professor at the Evangelical Lutheran Lyceum in 1838.

Italo Pizzi studied at the University of Pisa under Michele Kerbaker, Salvatore De Benedetti, Fausto Lasinio, and Emilio Teza. A scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indology fields, he taught at Florence, Naples, and Turin.

Itsuko Nishikawa is a linguistics and Japanology scholar who studied at Teachers College, Columbia University. Attested in 2026, she has served as a Teaching Professor at the University of Washington.

Ivan Ivanovich Zarubin was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and Kharkiv, later holding long-term posts at the Kunstkamera, Saint Petersburg State University, and the Institute of Linguistics.
Ivan Minayev was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University. He served on the Faculty of Oriental Studies there from around 1869 to 1890.

Ivan Pavlovich Minaev studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Vasily Vasiliev and Kaetan Andreevich Kossovich, and with Albrecht Weber. A scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies, he became a professor at Saint Petersburg State University in 1873.
Ivan Stchoukine was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Paul Pelliot and Alfred Foucher.

Ivanna Otroshchenko is a scholar of Buddhist, Iranian, Central Asian, and historical studies. She studied at Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv and became a Leading Research Fellow at the A. Yu. Krymskyi Institute of Oriental Studies in 1998.

Ivar Ulrik Wallenius studied at Katedralskolan i Åbo and the Royal Academy of Turku, where he became Docent of Arabic in 1817. A scholar of linguistics and Indology, he was Associate Professor at the University of Helsinki (1824–1852).

Ives Goddard was a linguist who studied at Harvard College and Harvard University. He held posts at Harvard University (circa 1966–1969), the Smithsonian Institution, and the National Museum of Natural History (circa 1970).
Ives Waldo is a scholar of philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Oxford and studied under Chögyam Trungpa from 1970 to 1988.

Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan is a scholar of Buddhist, Tibetan, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University, studying under Leonard van der Kuijp, Charles Hallisey, and Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and held a fellowship post at Grinnell College.

Ivo Fišer was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Vincenc Lesný and Oldřich Friš. He lectured at Charles University (attested 1960) and held a post at the University of Copenhagen (attested 1970).

Iwao Ishikawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Attested between 2000 and 2026, he has held posts at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Iwao Nakajima is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hitotsubashi University and under Nichiki Kimura. He held posts at the NHK Broadcasting Culture Research Institute until 1975 and at Sandhaan (attested 1999).
Iwao Shima was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Nagoya University. He served on the faculty at Kanazawa University, where he was a professor from around 1999 to 2007.

Izumi Hoshi is a Tibetologist and linguist who completed her undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Tokyo. She joined Tokyo University of Foreign Studies as an assistant professor in 1997 and served as director from 2019 to 2023.

Izumi Matsuda-Kiami is a scholar of Japanology and linguistics who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Attested in 2026, she has served as a Teaching Professor at the University of Washington.
